newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr closes stronger despite rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr closes stronger despite rate fears.

text.p: * Canada's dollar strengthened on Thursday to close at C$1.3502 (US$74.07) from Wednesday's close at C$1.3526 (US$.7394).
* Most of the strength came during brisk overnight trading overseas, dealers said. * They said fears of an ease in interest rates kept daytime trading in check.
The Canadian dollar firmed again on Thursday to close at C$1.3526 (US$.7394).
Dealers said most of the currency's strength came during brisk overnight trading overseas.
They said the currency hit its strongest levels in a year at around C$1.3488 (US$0.7413), during European trading.
Large trades in an illiquid market made for a volatile overnight market, said one trader.
Healthy corporate interest maintained the unit's strength during the day but trading was quiet, he said. The currency was held in check by fears of a possible Bank of Canada rate cut, dealers said.
But the tone of the unit was optimistic, they said.
"Everyday it seeems to look better and better," said one trader. "The general feeling is more and more people are coming back and trading the Canadian dollar. It's the beginning of a trend."
Strong economic fundamentals are encouraging investors to buy T-bills, which helps the Canadian dollar, he added.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 1.1313 marks from 1.1287 marks but dropped to 82.28 yen from 82.35 yen.
